label: 1.2.0-opus-high
messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- Phase: implement from a written spec, about 12 files
- Model and effort: `/model sonnet` then `/effort medium`
- Boundary: switch after `/clear`, and start from the spec file, not from memory. Changing model or effort on a warm context re-processes all of it, so the cost is your whole current context; `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so running it just before one costs least.
- Delegate: send test runs, log reading and any lookups of code the spec doesn't cover to subagents. To put those on Haiku, set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1`. Keep the implementation itself in the main session.
- Done when: the test suite and `npm run lint` (or the project's equivalent) pass, no test file was edited to get there, and each file the spec names has been changed as it says.
- You give up: at 12 files, Sonnet may miss connections between files or read an unclear part of the spec too literally. On the bench, Sonnet at medium passed every implement-from-spec run at 17% of the cost of Opus at xhigh, which also passed every run. That bench task was on a small test project, so a 12-file change goes beyond what it measured.
- Escalate when: if Sonnet skipped files, didn't run the tests or stopped partway, raise effort first (`/effort high`, then `xhigh`). If it had the right context and still got it wrong, move to `/model opus` at `medium`, then `xhigh`. For one hard turn, try `ultrathink` in that prompt before either move. Either switch re-processes a warm context, so write down where the work stands and `/clear` first. Ultracode doesn't fit here because the files depend on each other.

- Phase: review a six-file diff in a familiar repo
- Model and effort: `/model opus` then `/effort low`
- Boundary: `/clear` first, then switch. If you switch without clearing, your whole current context gets re-processed on the new model or effort (check its size with `/context`). This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one costs least.
- Delegate: nothing. The diff is small enough to read in the main context. Only push test runs or log reading to a subagent if the review needs them.
- Done when: every finding has a file:line and a concrete failing input or state, and you've checked each one against the code.
- You give up: coverage beyond the obvious. Low effort means fewer turns and less thinking, so an uncertain or subtle issue might not get chased down. On the bench's six-file diff, opus at low found all five planted defects in 3 turns. Opus at high found the same five in 13 turns at 3.3x the cost. Sonnet at high missed one defect in two runs of three, so dropping to Sonnet isn't the cheaper option here. That evidence is from `claude-opus-5` and `claude-sonnet-5`.
- Escalate when: the review misses something you can point to, or the diff turns out larger or less familiar than expected. Then go to `/effort high` on opus. If the review skipped files, raise effort. If it read everything and still got it wrong, change model. Ultracode isn't worth it on a six-file diff: on the bench it cost 9.5x `xhigh` for the same five defects.
